# K8.5 Grouped dy amax + dbias (+ FC2 dscales) in one pass

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `NVFP4_DY_STATS=1`, `NVFP4_DY_STATS_IMPL=cuda`,
`NVFP4_DY_STATS_FC2=1`, `NVFP4_DY_STATS_CUDA_FC2=1`, `NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_EXT`, `NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_COLS=448` ·
Class: **Bitwise** (amaxes, hence quantized bytes); no dbias or dscales in G6c (no expert bias) · Rule basis: TR-8.3

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

| | G6, G6b, G6c |
|---|---|
| Switches | `NVFP4_DY_STATS` L102, `NVFP4_DY_STATS_CUDA_FC2` L103, `NVFP4_DY_STATS_FC2` L104, `NVFP4_DY_STATS_IMPL=cuda` L105, `NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_EXT=/opt/nvfp4_ext/nvfp4_amax_dbias_ext.so` L84; `NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_COLS=448` L85 (columns per CTA of the unscaled variants; default 1024, V7 patch L834); `NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_COLS_SCALED` not set (256, L835) |
| Code | V7 patch `amax_dbias_ext.cu` L18-316, `nvfp4_amax_dbias.py` L776-856, Triton fallback `nvfp4_dy_stats.py` L857-1053, `grouped_mlp.py` L323-380, L438-453, L644-760 |
| Build | `nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/Dockerfile` L138-143 (`nvfp4_amax_dbias.build(..., arch='10.3')`, `-O3`, V7 patch L798-805) |

Same files in both packages and the same V7 patch in G6c.

## 2. What the reference does

In the grouped MLP backward (TE 27486e03 with the NVFP4 patch), the FC1 and FC2 output gradients
dy are quantized with TE's grouped NVFP4 quantize, whose `GraphSafeGroupHadamardAmaxTmaKernel`
computes per expert the pre-RHT row-wise amax and the post-RHT column-wise amax. The FC1 dbias
comes from TE's Triton grouped dbias (K5.8); the FC2 scaled dbias and dscales from
`compute_grouped_dbias_dscales` (V7 patch L710-719). Each reads dy again.

## 3. What this implementation does

1. `_dy_stats_for` (L359-380) returns (amax_row, amax_col, dbias, dscales) from one read of dy.
2. With `NVFP4_DY_STATS_IMPL=cuda` and `supported` (L824-831), it calls the extension
   `amax_dbias` (L838-856 → `.cu` L274-314). One CTA covers 64 rows × `cols_per_cta` columns.
3. Per 64×64 BF16 tile in shared memory (TE's swizzle), `mma_amax` multiplies by the 16×16
   Hadamard fragment, rounds to BF16 and takes `max.xorsign.abs` (L50-73, L183-193): TE's
   instruction sequence for both amaxes. The same tile gives the dbias column sums
   (L194-234) and, for FC2, `sum dy × scale` and dscales `sum dy × bias` (L203-225).
4. `_group_quantize_with_stats` (L438-453) quantizes dy with these amaxes through TE's
   `_group_quantize_with_amax_for_grouped_mlp`; FC2 at L654-676, FC1 at L727-757; FC2 dscales
   are added to `grad_scales` (L697-699).

G6c: the experts have no bias. FC2 calls `_dy_stats_for` with `dbias=False` and no scales (`not output_fc2_dbias`,
L655-665), FC1 with `dbias=fc1_op.has_bias` = False (L728-735). Both take the amax-only instantiation
`amax_dbias_kernel<false, false>` (`.cu` L310-311) with `cols_per_cta = min(448, hidden rounded up to 64)` (L834,
L843-845): 7 CTAs per 64-row block for the 2944-wide FC2 dy (the last covers 256 columns) and 14 for the 5888-wide
FC1 dy (the last covers 64). No dbias or dscales are computed, and `grad_scales` gets no dscales term (L697-699 needs
`scale_bias`).

## 4. Why the result is the same

- Amaxes: the same instructions on the same BF16 values; max is order-independent
  (`atomicMax` on non-negative floats, L264-265). Equal amaxes give equal quantized bytes.
  Bitwise.
- Column split: each CTA covers a multiple of 64 columns (`.cu` L138-141, checked at L291-292), and the amax is a
  max over all of them, so the 448-column split gives the same amax as any other split.
- dbias, dscales: the same sums in FP32 in a different order (per-warp rows, then four warp
  partials, then `atomicAdd` across CTAs, L230-232, L238-243). Same function. TE's Triton
  reference also accumulates with atomics; neither is repeatable call to call.

## 5. Numerics

FP32 accumulation; FC2 products with `fmaf` (L204-205, L221-222); dbias returned in FP32 and cast
to BF16 by the caller (L720). The precomputed-amax quantize does not all-reduce amaxes (L443-453),
as TE's grouped quantize does not either (comment L443-444).

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** `_dy_stats_for` (L361-370): switch on, more than one group, `NVFP4Quantizer` with
  RHT and post-RHT amax, BF16 dy. FC2 only if `NVFP4_DY_STATS_FC2` and (no FC2 dbias or scaled
  bias) (L654); FC1 only with NVFP4 and (`triton_fc1_dbias` or no FC1 bias) (L728). CUDA path:
  rows % 64, hidden % 64; FC2 also `NVFP4_DY_STATS_CUDA_FC2=1`, FP32 contiguous scales, BF16
  contiguous bias (L824-831); the extension re-checks and limits `cols_per_cta` (L278-293).
- **Falls back:** to the Triton `nvfp4_dy_stats` (L377-380) if the CUDA path is unsupported, or
  to TE's quantize and dbias paths if `_dy_stats_for` returns `None` (L677, L710-719, L740).
  Silent: no log line or counter.
- **Assumes:** (a) every expert's row offset is a multiple of 64 (`.cu` comment L271-272). The
  kernel takes the group of a CTA from its first row (L121-129) and does not check; a group
  starting inside a 64-row block would have its first rows counted in the previous group's amax
  and dbias. The MoE layout aligns every expert to 256 rows (K4.3 test, job 22307).
  (b) `NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_EXT` is set; `_get_ext` has no fallback (L811).
- **Check:** config L102-105, L84. The runs print nothing for this path.
- **Records available on request** (not in the package): image verify jobs 22541 and 22589 on the G6b image (same patches and `Dockerfile`; not repeated on this image): `nvfp4_amax_dbias.py`, `nvfp4_dy_stats.py` `== production
  overlay`, `/opt/nvfp4_ext/nvfp4_amax_dbias_ext.so loads (1 symbols)`.

## 7. Code

V7 patch L18-316 (`amax_dbias_ext.cu`), L776-856 (`nvfp4_amax_dbias.py`), L857-1053
(`nvfp4_dy_stats.py`), `grouped_mlp.py` hunks L321-453 and L644-760; `nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/Dockerfile` L138-143.

## 8. Tests and evidence

Kernel tests on the image (Firmus test scripts, available on request; installed module and
`.so`):
- On this package's image, `k8_5_dy_stats`, job 22880, with the package config sourced (`NVFP4_AMAX_DBIAS_COLS=448`):
  60 cases per run, 0 differ except the 2 fixtures (column amax off by 2⁻¹⁰: 2 715 548 and 1 352 979 elements),
  captured inputs of this package's training run (job 22873) included; run a vs b 200 equal, 0 differ. The test
  calls the dbias variants (`dbias=True`, plain and scaled); the amax-only instantiation that this package runs is
  not called by it (section 9). The G6 results follow.

- `k8_5_dy_stats`, job 22497, runs a and b rc 0, 60 cases per run. Reference `tex.group_quantize`
  (TE computes the amaxes), round to nearest. Amax row and column, row- and column-wise data
  and scales: 0 differ, including 7 captured layers × 2 iterations × widths 5888 (FC1, plain)
  and 2944 (FC2, scaled) with the real expert layout. The 2 cases with a difference are the
  fixtures (column amax off by 2^-10): 2 715 548 (5888) and 1 352 979 (2944) elements. Run a vs
  run b: 200 equal, 0 differ.
- dbias and dscales vs FP64 (test `k8_5_dy_stats`, job 22179): shipped and upstream
  `compute_grouped_dbias_dscales` errors of the same size, relative L2 in the 1e-7 range;
  3 distinct digests in 3 calls for dbias (shipped and upstream) and for shipped dscales.
- Supported widths (job 22416): 2880, 3008, 5824, 5952, 4096 yes; 2928, 2960 no.
- `k5_7_k5_8_variants`, job 22414, grouped MLP forward and backward: `NVFP4_DY_STATS=0` vs the
  shipped setting differs in 3-44 of 132-196 outputs per case (13-69 elements, one case 65 561);
  the shipped-vs-shipped control differs in 3-35 outputs (one case 32 776). The switch adds no
  difference beyond the run-to-run variation of the atomics.

## 9. Open points

1. The per-case FP64 errors (max abs, relative L2) of job 22497 are in the JSONL test records
   (available on request); only "1e-7 range" (job 22179) is quoted here.
2. No scored-run evidence that the CUDA path (not the Triton or TE fallback) ran; a counter
   printed once would close this.
3. The amax-only kernel (`kDbias=false`) that G6c runs is not compared directly by `k8_5_dy_stats`. Its amax code is
   the same template code as the tested variants, with the dbias block compiled out (`if constexpr (kDbias)`,
   `.cu` L194-234); the grouped-MLP tests on this image (K4.1, K5.9: jobs 22907, 22908) run it inside the backward
   but do not isolate it.
